title: App onboarding and feature discoverability issues for Garmin users (CL-0033)
problem_statement: Several users report that the app is initially confusing and that it does not explain many of its features well, requiring users to figure things out on their own or look externally for guidance. This onboarding and feature-clarity problem is observed alongside otherwise positive sentiment about the app's functionality (e.g., syncing with Garmin watches, run tracking for XC/track season, graphs, regular updates). The cluster contains 7 feedback items with a maximum severity of S3 and a priority score of 43.
root_cause_hypotheses: Hypothesis 1: In-app onboarding flow is missing or insufficient — new users encounter the app's full feature set without guided introduction, leading to confusion noted in F0095 and F0123.

Hypothesis 2: Feature descriptions, labels, or in-app help/tooltips are absent or unclear, so users cannot self-serve answers about what features do, as suggested by F0123's statement that the app 'doesn't explain a lot of the features well'.

Hypothesis 3: Users rely on external context (e.g., XC/track season workflows in F0115, F0231) that the app does not surface or contextualize, so the gap between user goals and UI clarity is most visible for use cases like mileage tracking with Garmin Forerunner devices.
counter_evidence: ["F0218 explicitly states 'No faults at all, syncs well' and praises graphs and regular updates, contradicting a general 'app is broken' framing — the issue is not universal and may be limited to new or specific-use-case users.", "F0232 shows a long-tenured user ('almost ten years') with 'No complaints', indicating the onboarding/feature-clarity gap does not affect experienced users and may be transient after initial learning (consistent with F0095's 'got the hang of it pretty quickly').", "F0115 and F0231 are net-positive reviews where the onboarding complaint is not raised; the relevant common factor is Garmin + XC/track usage rather than the app's general onboarding flow, which weakens the case for a broad onboarding redesign vs. targeted use-case guidance.", 'No quantitative data on churn, drop-off, or support tickets is present in the provided evidence, so the business impact of the onboarding/feature-clarity issue cannot be confirmed from this cluster alone.']

recommended_actions.action: Add or revise a first-run onboarding flow that introduces core features (e.g., syncing with a Garmin watch, tracking runs, viewing graphs) with short, contextual walkthroughs, addressing the 'confusing at first' feedback in F0095.

Audit feature copy, labels, and empty states across the app and add in-context tooltips or 'Learn more' links for features users flag as unexplained (per F0123), with a focus on Garmin device pairing and run-tracking screens.

Create a short in-app help section or FAQ covering common use cases such as XC/track season mileage tracking with Garmin Forerunner devices (referenced in F0115, F0231), so users have a first-party resource instead of guessing.
Triage and communicate the intermittent issues referenced in F0211 ('when it works'); reducing reliability flakiness will lower perceived onboarding friction for new users who hit a failure early.
Validate changes by re-surveying users who reported onboarding confusion (F0095, F0123) and tracking time-to-first-successful-sync or time-to-first-meaningful-action as a leading indicator.

problem_statement: 簇 CL-0041 下仅含 FID F0135 一条证据，提示心率监测功能在用户进行 minimal effort（极低强度运动）时段，会出现 'sometimes way overcounts beats for stretches of time' 的现象，即在长时间段内将心率 beats 显著高估。该问题被定级为 S3（最高严重度），簇优先级分数为 16，表明虽仅一条反馈，但严重度高、影响持续时间长，需优先排查。

运动/活动识别模块未将 'minimal effort' 状态正确切回静息或低强度模式，心率估算仍沿用运动补偿模型，造成 beats 被惯性放大。
信号去噪与峰值检测参数（最小峰间隔、阈值）在低幅度脉搏波下不适用，低强度段的微弱 R 波/脉搏波被多次计为多个 beat。
counter_evidence: ["簇内仅 1 条证据（F0135），样本量极小，尚不能确认 'minimal effort 段持续过计数' 是普遍现象还是个别设备/佩戴条件下的孤立问题。", "证据原文描述为用户主观感受（'not always accurate'、'sometimes way overcounts'），未提供具体心率数值、持续秒数或参考基准，'way overcounts' 的实际偏差幅度未知，可能被体感放大。", '未明确指出该问题是出现在整段 minimal effort 内，还是仅出现在高强度向低强度过渡的窗口期；若为后者，则根因可能集中在过渡处理而非稳态 minimal effort 段，需进一步澄清。', '未给出运动类型、设备型号、固件版本等信息，无法排除特定硬件/固件组合的兼容性因素。', '在进一步数据复核前，不应假设 minimal effort 段必然系统性过计数；若实测显示偏差在可接受范围内，则当前 S3 定级与优先级分数 16 需重新评估。']

title: App-Hardware Pairing & Connectivity Instability (HRM Pro)
problem_statement: Users experience severe reliability problems pairing the application with the HRM Pro device, including failed updates, slow connection times, and a recurring need to unpair/repair or factory-reset a ~$700 watch within roughly a year of ownership. Sentiment across the 3-cluster is strongly negative, with explicit comparisons of software quality being 'utter garbage' and disbelief at the poor performance.
root_cause_hypotheses: Bluetooth pairing/handshake state machine fails to recover gracefully, forcing users to manually unpair and re-pair.
Firmware/app version compatibility drift causes the device to drop connection or fail to apply over-the-air updates.
Inadequate session persistence or token/caching logic leads to repeated re-authentication on each launch.
counter_evidence: ['The cluster contains only 3 verbatim comments; the high-severity S3 rating is driven by tone rather than by volume or quantified failure rate.', 'No telemetry, logs, or reproduction steps are attached to the source feedback, so frequency and root-cause attribution are inferred, not measured.', 'Cost-of-device framing in F0230 may amplify perceived severity but is itself anecdotal and not necessarily indicative of a defect rate.', 'HRM Pro vs. broader HRM hardware/software complaints are not distinguished; the issue could be app-wide rather than specific to HRM Pro.']

recommended_actions.action: Capture device logs from users reproducing the unpair/repair loop to identify the exact handshake failure point and recovery state.
Audit and harden the BLE pairing/reconnect state machine to auto-recover from failed handshakes without requiring manual unpair or factory reset.
Validate firmware-to-app version compatibility matrix and add an in-app diagnostic that surfaces blocking version mismatches before update attempts.
Run a warranty/RMA cohort analysis on HRM Pro units sold in the last 12 months to determine whether a hardware defect subset is inflating software-side complaints.
Add a guided in-app troubleshooting flow (re-pair, reset, contact support) triggered automatically after repeated connection failures to reduce user effort.
